title: ～から (〜kara)
shortExplanation: Express a reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
longExplanation: The ～から grammar point is used to express a reason, cause, or the origin of something. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'due to' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + から, い-Adjective + から, な-Adjective + だから, Noun + だから

examples.jp: 雨が降るから、傘を持って行ってください。
examples.romaji: Ame ga furu kara, kasa wo motte itte kudasai.
examples.en: Because it's raining, please bring an umbrella.

examples.jp: このケーキは美味しいから、みんな食べるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa oishii kara, minna taberu deshou.
examples.en: Because this cake is delicious, everyone will probably eat it.

examples.jp: 彼は病気だから、学校を休みます。
examples.romaji: Kare wa byouki dakara, gakkou wo yasumimasu.
examples.en: He will be absent from school because he is sick.

examples.jp: 今日は日曜日だから、学校がありません。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa nichiyoubi dakara, gakkou ga arimasen.
examples.en: There is no school today because it is Sunday.

usageNote: Everyday spoken default for stating a reason; emphasizes the speaker's subjective reason. (Near-duplicate of n5-073 - same word/register, taught at both N4 and N5.)
